I found no compliance violations in PR #70, so there are no issues to report.

- **ADR content rule:** ADRs 0020 and 0021 contain no code or implementation details. The terms they use, such as "GHCR package", "cache tags" and "untagged version", name behavior, not code.
- **Superseded ADRs:** The PR supersedes no ADR. ADR 0020 lists the earlier fork behavior under "Considered Options" and says it was never recorded, so there is nothing to delete.
- **ADR conflicts:** I found no contradiction with an existing ADR, and the new ADRs don't conflict with each other.
- **Code comments:** The added comments in `images.yml` and `docker-bake.hcl` each state a constraint or reason. The `docker-bake.hcl` comments cover the `CACHE` and `PLATFORM` dependency, and `mode=max` and `image-manifest=true`. None restates the code.
- **Glossary:** The glossary defines no term the PR needs, and the PR doesn't use a glossary term in a way that drifts from its definition.
- **PR body rule:** I did not check the PR body for diffs or file lists, because the checklist is scoped to the diff and repo conventions.

One observation that does not rise to a rule violation: ADR 0020 and ADR 0021 head the section "Considered Options" with a capital O. Most existing ADRs, and the `AGENTS.md` wording, use "Considered options". ADR 0019 uses the capital form, so the repo is already inconsistent. No quotable rule covers heading case, so I'm not raising it.

No compliance violations found. I read the diff and the repo's ADRs and README, and did not execute anything.

- **ADR content:** ADRs 0020 and 0021 contain no code, diffs or file listings. They state decisions and consequences only. ADR 0020 is the only place the PR touches the old fork behaviour, and it lists that behaviour under "Considered Options" even though nothing is being superseded. No ADR is superseded, so no deletion is required.
- **Heading case:** both new ADRs use "## Considered Options". Existing ADRs mix "Considered options" (10 files) and "Considered Options" (3 files, including 0019). AGENTS.md quotes "Considered options" only for superseded ADRs, so this is not a quotable violation.
- **README:** the PR adds three lines, and the README is 100 lines, so it stays brief.
- **Comments:** the added comments in `images/docker-bake.hcl` and `.github/workflows/images.yml` each state a constraint (per-architecture cache, GHCR manifest rejection, `edge` not moving on manual runs). None restates the code.
- **PR description:** it contains no diffs and no file lists.

I did not check `GLOSSARY.md` vocabulary beyond the ADR and README text.

Issues: none.

I found one issue, and it does not block. Nothing else in the two code files looked like a bug; I checked the points listed after the finding.

**1. Ubuntu packages stay frozen in the build cache, so published images stop picking up security fixes**
- **File:** `images/docker-bake.hcl`, lines 40-49 (the cache functions are used by every target at lines 64-65, 74-75, 84-85, 94-95). Turned on in `.github/workflows/images.yml` line 96, `CACHE: true`.
- **Quoted added text:** `result = CACHE ? ["type=registry,ref=${cache_ref(name)},mode=max,image-manifest=true,oci-mediatypes=true"] : []`
- **Reason:** bug (behavioral regression)
- **Description:** Three images install packages from Ubuntu's archive without pinning a version: `images/core/Dockerfile`, `images/core-systemd/Dockerfile`, and `coder-template` through its parents. That covers `ca-certificates curl git gnupg sudo ...`, `python3`, `systemd dbus libpam-systemd ...`, and `containerd.io`, which the core Dockerfile explicitly says "floats". BuildKit decides whether a `RUN` step can come from cache only by its command text and parent layer, never by what the network would return now. With `cache-from`/`cache-to` on every run, that install step is served from `cache-<arch>` until the Dockerfile line or the `ubuntu:26.04@sha256:` base changes. Before this PR, every build that ran reinstalled these packages fresh. Every `main` run moves `edge` on all four images together, so it will now republish the old package set while looking like a fresh build. ADR 0021 doesn't mention this trade-off.
- **Trigger:** A push to `main` that changes only `images/coder-template/run-in-tmux` (it passes the `images/**` filter). Since the cache was last filled, Ubuntu has shipped a security update for `sudo`, `curl` or `systemd`, or Docker has shipped a new `containerd.io`.
- **Path:** `.github/workflows/images.yml@build` "Build every image…" step (`CACHE: true`) → `images/docker-bake.hcl@cache_from` / `@cache_to` → `images/core/Dockerfile@RUN apt-get update && apt-get install …` hits the cache → `images/core-systemd/Dockerfile@RUN apt-get update && apt-get install systemd …` hits the cache → `.github/workflows/images.yml@publish` "Tag every image for both architectures" moves `edge` onto those digests.
- **Outcome:** `edge` (and `pr-N`) for `core`, `core-systemd`, `coder-template` and `devcontainer-base` are republished with outdated, possibly vulnerable Ubuntu and `containerd.io` packages. Without the cache, the same run would have installed the current versions.
- **Suggested fix:** Pick one of these:
  - Make the install steps change when the archive changes, for example with an `ARG` set to the date that CI passes in.
  - Leave the apt layers out of the cache with `no-cache-filter`.
  - Write down in ADR 0021 that floating packages refresh only when the base digest is bumped, and make sure Renovate bumps the `ubuntu:26.04` digest often enough.
- **Blocks:** no. Nothing in the code shows whether this was intended, so the author should confirm.

**Checked and dismissed (for the human report):**
- **`PUBLISH` and `publish.if` rewrite:** gives the same result as before for pushes to `main`, `main` runs started by hand, and pull requests from this repository's own branches. A manual run on another branch still evaluates to false.
- **Fork pull requests:** they now fail, because the read-only token can't write the cache and publishing is attempted. ADR 0020 and the PR description say this is intended, so I didn't raise it.
- **`ghcr-cleanup.yml` and `stale-pr-tags.sh`:** they match only `^pr-[0-9]+$` and delete only the tags listed, so the `cache-*` tags are never deleted. Old caches pile up as untagged versions, which ADR 0021 acknowledges.
- **Pull requests and `main` writing the same `cache-<arch>` tag at the same time:** the last write wins. That's harmless and stated in the ADR.
- **The first run, before any cache exists:** the importer reports "not found" and the build carries on.
- **`images.sh` parent-first order:** unaffected, because the cache adds no `contexts` entries.
- **Test coverage gap:** nothing checks the `bake --print` output with and without `CACHE`. The PR's test plan says this was checked by hand. Not a blocker.

I found 2 findings in the changed docs, and neither blocks. I ran the durable-knowledge audit in diff mode, report-only, over the added lines in `README.md`, `docs/adr/0020-pull-requests-from-collaborators-only.md` and `docs/adr/0021-build-cache-in-the-registry.md`. I also checked the code comments the diff adds in `.github/workflows/images.yml` and `images/docker-bake.hcl`.

No ADR is superseded by this PR. No existing ADR covers forks or a CI build cache: ADR 0014 mentions a build cache, but it is about engine storage volumes, which is a different decision. So the "delete superseded ADRs" rule is satisfied. The old fork behaviour was never an ADR, and ADR 0020 already lists it under Considered Options.

## Findings

**1. `docs/adr/0020-pull-requests-from-collaborators-only.md`, line 9**
- Quoted added text: `- Forks build and test without publishing (the previous behaviour, never recorded as an ADR).`
- Verdict: **REWRITE**. Remove the parenthetical, which records history, and keep the option: `- Forks build and test without publishing.`
- Rule: under the skill's "Durable vs not", the parenthetical records how things used to be and whether they were written down. That does not survive a rewrite. AGENTS.md asks for the old decision to be listed under "Considered options", and the bullet without the parenthetical already does that. Nothing is lost: the old behaviour is still described by the line the diff deletes from `.github/workflows/images.yml` ("Forks build and test only").
- Blocks: no.

**2. `README.md`, lines 19–20 (added), which conflict with line 16 (unchanged)**
- Quoted added text: `The \`cache-amd64\` and \`cache-arm64\` tags are CI's build cache, not images to pull.`
- Verdict: **REWRITE**. Line 16 still says "The only tags are `edge` (…) and `pr-N`", and the added sentence then introduces two more tags, so the README contradicts itself. Change line 16 to "The only image tags are `edge` … and `pr-N`" and keep the added sentence as it is. Or fold the cache tags into that sentence as the exception.
- Rule: README.md must be "Keep[ed] current as the repo evolves" (AGENTS.md).
- Blocks: no.

## Dismissed candidates (logged for human review, as AGENTS.md requires)

- **ADR 0021 line 8**, "The GitHub Actions cache: capped in size, evicts, and is scoped per branch." This claims how a third-party tool behaves. I kept it as the reason that option was rejected. It is not code implementation detail, but it is not checkable offline either.
- **ADR 0021 line 15**, "A superseded cache stays as an untagged version, like the other untagged images the cleanup keeps." Kept. `.github/workflows/ghcr-cleanup.yml` confirms it: "Untagged images are kept: one edge moved off looks the same as one a failed run left behind."
- **ADR 0021 lines 3–4**, the decision statement (cache per architecture in the image's own GHCR package; read and written by every CI run; not used locally). Kept: it is decision-level and names no tags or options.
- **ADR 0020 lines 3–5**, "…a pull request from a fork fails its checks." Kept: it follows from the head commit, where `PUBLISH` is true for any `pull_request` and every run writes the cache to GHCR. I did not confirm it by running anything.
- **README lines 34–35**, the statement that the repo takes no outside contributions, with a link to ADR 0020. Kept: it is brief and the detail lives in the ADR, so the README rule is respected.
- **`images/docker-bake.hcl`**, the added comment "image-manifest=true: GHCR rejects the default cache index." This is a third-party behaviour claim I can't confirm offline. I kept it because it states a constraint (why the option is there), which is what AGENTS.md wants comments to do. "mode=max: also cache the layers of intermediate stages" sits on the line just before it and comes close to restating what the option does; I dropped it as below the bar.
- **`images/docker-bake.hcl`**, "# CI sets CACHE=true; needs PLATFORM, since each architecture has its own cache." Kept: it states a constraint.
- **`.github/workflows/images.yml`**, "# A manual run on another branch must not move edge." and "# Every run reads and writes the build cache in GHCR, publishing or not." Kept: each explains a condition the code cannot show by itself.

I found one issue in the PR, and it does not block. Nothing else in the two code files holds up as a wrong outcome or a security exposure.

### Issue 1: the cache keeps apt packages from updating, contrary to ADR 0013 and the README

- **File:** `images/docker-bake.hcl`, new-side lines 40–49 (used at lines 64–65, 74–75, 84–85, 94–95). It is turned on at `.github/workflows/images.yml` line 96.
- **Added text:** `result = CACHE ? ["type=registry,ref=${cache_ref(name)}"] : []` and `CACHE: true`
- **Reason:** logic. It touches security because the stuck packages include security fixes.
- **Description:** The Dockerfiles install unpinned apt packages:
  - `images/core/Dockerfile` installs ca-certificates, curl, git, gnupg, sudo, tmux and others, then python3, then `containerd.io` (its comment says "containerd.io floats").
  - `images/core-systemd/Dockerfile` installs systemd, dbus and libpam-systemd.

  BuildKit decides a cache hit from the command text and the layer below it, not from what the network returns. So once the cache holds a `RUN apt-get update && apt-get install …` layer, every later run reuses it. That includes `main` runs that move `edge`. ADR 0013 ("Apt packages … float within the Ubuntu release, so a rebuild can pick up newer ones") and the README ("Apt packages … float within the Ubuntu release") both describe the old behaviour. Before this PR, every `main` build rebuilt every layer, so any image change also refreshed all apt packages. ADR 0021 doesn't mention this trade-off.
- **Trigger:** a push to `main` that changes any file under `images/`, for example a Renovate bump of `CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION`. The `FROM ubuntu:26.04@sha256:…` digest and the apt `RUN` lines stay the same, and Ubuntu has shipped a security update since the cache was filled.
- **Path:** `.github/workflows/images.yml@build` ("Build every image of this commit…" step, `CACHE: true`) → `images/docker-bake.hcl@cache_from` → `images/docker-bake.hcl@target "core"` `cache-from` → `images/core/Dockerfile` first `RUN apt-get update` is a cache hit → `.github/workflows/images.yml@publish` tags `edge`.
- **Outcome:** `edge` ships the apt packages from whichever run first wrote the cache. The patched versions are skipped even though the image was rebuilt, and `containerd.io` stops floating. Only a change to the base-image digest (or to an earlier layer) refreshes them. Each image's children inherit the same stale layer.
- **Suggested fix:** pick one.
  - Make apt refresh on a known schedule, e.g. a scheduled `main` build with `--no-cache-filter` for the stages that run apt, or a date-based build arg on the apt `RUN` lines.
  - Or accept the trade-off explicitly: record in ADR 0021 that apt packages now update only when the base digest is bumped, and replace ADR 0013's apt consequence, since the PR contradicts it.
- **Blocks:** no. How stale the packages get is limited by how often Renovate bumps the Ubuntu base digest. Still, the PR contradicts ADR 0013 without saying so, which the domain rules ask to be raised explicitly.

### Dismissed candidates (logged as AGENTS.md requires)

1. **Cache poisoning from pull requests into `main`/`edge`** (`.github/workflows/images.yml` line 84 login now always runs, line 96 `CACHE: true`). PR runs write the same `cache-<arch>` tag that `main` reads. Dismissed because it opens no new hole:
   - A same-repo `pull_request` run already had `packages: write` before this PR. Its author can edit `images.yml` in the branch and push `edge` directly.
   - Without editing the workflow, a PR can't put different content under a cache key `main` will hit, because the keys depend on the commands, build args and copied files.
   - Fork runs get a read-only token, so they can't write the cache.
2. **Fork PRs now fail** (PUBLISH at line 20, `publish` `if` at line 128, the login no longer limited to publishing runs). A fork run's read-only token can't export the cache or push by digest, so the build fails and `publish` is skipped. ADR 0020 and the PR body say this is intended, and nothing is exposed.
3. **`PUBLISH` rewritten** at line 20. Same result as before for push to `main`, dispatch on `main`, dispatch on another branch (false, so `edge` doesn't move) and same-repo PRs. The only difference is forks, covered in item 2.
4. **PR and `main` runs racing on the cache tag** (`concurrency` is per ref). The last writer wins, which costs speed and never correctness. ADR 0021 already lists it.
5. **Cleanup and retention** (`.github/workflows/ghcr-cleanup.yml`, `.github/scripts/stale-pr-tags.sh`). The `sed` only matches `^pr-N$`, so cache tags are never chosen for deletion. Each run leaves untagged superseded cache versions that are kept forever; ADR 0021 already states this and no wrong result follows.
6. **`cache_ref` with an empty `PLATFORM`** would produce a `:cache-` tag. It can't happen: `CACHE` defaults to false locally, and CI always sets `PLATFORM`.
7. **Cancelled PR runs** (`cancel-in-progress`) leaving a half-written cache. The registry exporter pushes the layer blobs before the manifest, so a cancelled run leaves the old cache in place.

CONFIRM — Every part holds. The `images/**` paths filter lets a push to `main` through. `CACHE: true` makes `cache_from` read the registry cache for every target. The `core` Dockerfile's unpinned `RUN apt-get update && apt-get install …` layers (the `FROM` is digest-pinned) are then reused while their instructions are unchanged. `publish` tags `edge` on those digests, so `edge` carries the apt versions from whichever run filled the cache. ADR 0013 and the README say apt packages float so that a rebuild can pick up newer ones, but ADR 0021 doesn't mention that the cache holds them in place. The ADR 0013 contradiction is mild, since it says a rebuild "can" pick up newer versions, but the staleness itself is real and the PR doesn't surface it.

DROP: the parenthetical does record history, but it also says that forks building and testing without publishing was the old behaviour and that no ADR covered it. A reader needs that to see why the option is listed, and nothing in the rules forbids it. It is also a small, ambiguous point, not a clear violation.

DROP — the cache-tag sentence is in the same paragraph as "The only tags are `edge` … and `pr-N`", and the surrounding text is about pulled images, so "tags" there reads as image tags. The next sentence says the cache tags are not images to pull, so this is a wording nit, not a clear violation.

review.body:
The registry build cache and the collaborators-only scope are wired consistently. `PUBLISH` and the `publish` job condition behave as before for `main` and same-repo pull requests, and a manual run on another branch still leaves `edge` alone. `cache-*` tags are outside the stale-tag cleanup, and ADRs 0020 and 0021 record both decisions.

One non-blocking finding is inline: with the cache on, unpinned apt packages no longer refresh on rebuilds. Please either record that trade-off or add a way to refresh them.

comments.body:
**Non-blocking: apt packages stop floating once they are cached.** BuildKit decides a cache hit from the instruction text and its parent layer, not from what the apt archive serves now.

- **Trigger:** a push to `main` that changes anything under `images/` while the `ubuntu:26.04@sha256:…` base and the `apt-get install` lines stay the same, after Ubuntu or Docker's repo has shipped updates (for example a `sudo`, `curl` or `systemd` security fix, or a new `containerd.io`).
- **Path:** `.github/workflows/images.yml@build` (`CACHE: true`) → `images/docker-bake.hcl@cache_from` → the unpinned `RUN apt-get update && apt-get install …` layers in `images/core/Dockerfile` and `images/core-systemd/Dockerfile` come from `cache-<arch>` → `.github/workflows/images.yml@publish` moves `edge` onto those digests.
- **Outcome:** `edge` and `pr-N` ship the package versions of whichever run first filled the cache. Before this PR every build installed current versions. Now only a base-digest bump, or an edit to an earlier layer, refreshes them.

ADR 0013 and the README say apt packages float within the release so a rebuild can pick up newer ones, and ADR 0021 doesn't mention that the cache stops this. Either record the trade-off in ADR 0021 (packages refresh only when the base digest moves, so Renovate's digest bumps set how stale they can get), or keep packages fresh. Two ways to do that:

- a date-based build arg referenced in the apt `RUN` steps;
- a periodic `main` build that bypasses the cache for those stages, for example with `no-cache-filter`.
